findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:0 verificationEvidence command field (transition-orchestrator.ts) records grep -n "persistClaim = acquireMkdirLock|store.writeChecklist(args.storyId, reopenChecklist)|store.writeStory(args.storyId, story)|persistClaim.release()" packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts with a bare | for alternation. Confirmed by running it verbatim in this worktree (no output) vs with -E added (matches all four lines as described). The underlying factual claims in the note are independently verified TRUE (I re-derived the same line numbers, the single REOPEN assignment site at line 651, PHASE_EVENT_BY_TARGET lacking REOPEN, and store.writeJsonFile tmp+rename at store.ts:133-145), so this is not a coverage gap -- it is a reproducibility/hygiene defect in the recorded command string of an otherwise-adequate docs_check evidence entry.
findings.resolvedReason: Re-recorded CHK-002:happy:0 verificationEvidence with a reproducible command: grep -Fn with one -e per literal (replace-in-place confirmed at checklist.ts:934-937; exactly 1 entry, no duplicate). The stored string was extracted back out of checklist.json and executed verbatim: exit 0, exactly the four claimed lines 859/935/937/940. findings.desc: plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts:266,299,302,314 use 4 unnecessary `as any` casts ((e as any).fromPhase/.toPhase, reopenEvents[0] as any) on the new reopen-persistence + normal-transition-shape assertions. ProcessEvent (core/types.ts) already declares `[key: string]: unknown`, so `e.fromPhase` / `e.toPhase` / `reopenEvents[0].transitionType` resolve to `unknown` without any cast, and `unknown` compares/assigns fine against string literals in assert.equal/hasOwnProperty.call under this project's strict tsconfig. Verified empirically: in an isolated scratch git-worktree copy (separate from the shared REVIEW worktree/dist per the concurrency-hazard note) I removed all 4 casts, ran `npm --prefix packages/main run build` (tsc, strict) -> 0 errors, and reran `node packages/main/dist/tasks/plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js` -> both smoke assertions still pass unchanged. So the casts add no compile-time necessity; they just suppress the (already-weak, index-signature-typed) safety net for no benefit. Low severity: test-only file, no behavior difference, `as any` here does not actually widen acceptance beyond what the index signature already allows (a property-name typo would still silently type-check either way) so this is a minor precision/hygiene cleanup rather than a masked-typo risk.
findings.resolvedReason: Removed all 4 unnecessary `as any` casts from plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts (266/299/302/314); ProcessEvent already declares [key: string]: unknown so plain property access type-checks under strict tsconfig. Verified on the real tree: grep -n "as any" returns nothing, build exits 0, plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js and flow-stability-smoke.js both exit 0. Assertions semantically identical.

findings.desc: Cross-host review round B-70a6-xhr-r1/r2: independent host codex-host-b returned decision=fail with one MAJOR finding (recorded here by the main agent for tracking; the authoritative verdict is the host_verdict process event, not this record). Finding: "New reopen audit semantics are absent from the process-fact contract" at packages/main/src/core/process-fact-registry.ts:1371. This story makes transitionType and reason durable semantics of PLAN->INIT phase_transition events, but the registered phase-transition process fact still describes only fromPhase/toPhase/attemptId/reviewRound/materialHash/storyFilesHash, and scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs has no assertion for the new fields. That violates the CLAUDE.md dual-layer process-fact contract (prompt guidance + hardcoded mechanical fallback) and lets a later refactor silently drop the reopen marker or the reason while the mechanical contract still passes - defeating the audit guarantee this story exists to establish. Fix: extend the runtime phase-transition process-fact declaration to cover the REOPEN marker + reason semantics, and extend verify-process-fact-contract.mjs to mechanically assert that a successful REOPEN emits transitionType=reopen with the validated reason while ordinary transitions omit both fields. Note: all three local Claude reviewers (concept, quality, test-coverage) passed without catching this; the independent host did.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit b964aa7619, addressing the MAJOR finding raised by independent host codex-host-b in cross-host rounds r1/r2. (1) packages/main/src/core/process-fact-registry.ts: the runtime:closeout_phase_transition entry now declares the reopen audit semantics - transitionType='reopen' as the backward-reopen marker and reason as the already-validated operator reason (>= REOPEN_REASON_MIN), both strictly additive and set ONLY on REOPEN, with ordinary transitions omitting them. Declared honestly as audit-only history, NOT gate evidence, since nothing currently consumes it; the implementer explicitly declined to over-claim it as gate-consumed. (2) scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs: new assertPhaseTransitionReopenAuditContract(), called beside assertCloseoutTrustBoundary(), following the file's existing registry-token plus AST-anchored source assertion style (source-first by design so a stale dist cannot hide drift). It asserts four layers: the builder emits each field only via a real input.<field> !== undefined spread with an empty else; the call site gates on a real eventType === REOPEN condition emitting exactly transitionType 'reopen' plus args.reason, with an empty object on the ordinary branch; the PLAN->INIT remap keeps a throwing REOPEN_REASON_MIN branch so the persisted reason is the validated one; and the two executable smokes keep their end-to-end assertions. RED PROOF (isolated filesystem copy, deleted afterwards, so the shared worktree git state was never perturbed): scratch baseline exit 0, then 7 mutations each producing exit 1 and each restored - remove the call-site REOPEN gate; drop reason; rename the marker to 'REOPEN'; make the ordinary branch emit undefined fields; make the builder emit transitionType unconditionally; delete the reason validation; revert the registry rationale. For the primary mutation the full path was run: the mutated tree COMPILES CLEAN (npm --prefix packages/main run build exit 0, proving tsc cannot catch this class of regression) while npm run test:process-fact-contract exits 1 with the message that the call site must gate the reopen audit fields on a real eventType === REOPEN condition; reverting flips it back to exit 0, proving the failure is caused by the mutation rather than the scratch environment. Post-change verification on the shared worktree: build exit 0, test:process-fact-contract exit 0 ('Process fact contract verified'), plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke exit 0, flow-stability-smoke exit 0. This closes the dual-layer process-fact gap: the audit guarantee this story establishes can no longer be silently refactored away while the mechanical contract keeps passing.

findings.desc: Cross-host review round B-70a6-xhr-r3: independent host codex-host-b returned decision=fail with a second MAJOR finding (recorded by the main agent for tracking; the authoritative verdict is the host_verdict process event). Finding: 'Reopen state is persisted before its required audit event' at packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:950. VERIFIED against source: store.writeStory persists phase=INIT at line 937, the persist claim is released in the finally at line 940, and store.appendProcessEvent runs at line 950 OUTSIDE the claim. If the append throws or the process dies in that window, the reopen HAS happened but no transitionType/reason audit record exists - and because REOPEN can only fire from PLAN, the story has already left the only phase that could retry it, so the event is UNRECOVERABLE. This defeats the durable audited-reopen guarantee that is the entire point of this story. It also matches the requester's own stated acceptance standard: a successful PLAN->INIT transition must produce exactly one audit event containing the full reason, and a failed transition must leave no event claiming success. NOTE ON PROCESS: the main agent previously argued this concern was merely a pre-existing universal property of all transitions and excluded it from scope. That reasoning was WRONG - the mechanism is universal but the unrecoverability is specific to REOPEN, because the transition moves the story out of its only valid source phase. Fix direction (per the requester's prescribed remedy of prepared/committed state plus failure recovery): persist the reopen reason ATOMICALLY with the phase write via the story index single tmp-write+rename, then append the event, then clear the record; reconcile a missing event on a later read/transition so a crash leaves a recoverable state rather than an unaudited reopen. Update the process-fact registry and verifier to cover the recovery semantics.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 9ead1958c8. The reopen's audit facts (auditId, verbatim reason, fromPhase, hashes, reviewRound) are now attached to the story object BEFORE the persist claim, so they land in the SAME writeStory tmp-write+renameSync as phase=INIT - one atomic rename, meaning either the reopen did not commit at all or it committed with its reason durable. reconcilePendingReopenAudit() emits any missing event and clears the record, and runs at the top of EVERY transition, giving the load-bearing invariant: no phase change can follow an unaudited reopen. Idempotency is exact reopenAuditId identity rather than reason text (two reopens may legitimately share a reason); the clear happens only after the event is durable; the same function serves both the normal and recovery paths so they cannot drift. Ordinary transitions have pendingReopenAudit absent and keep a byte-identical event shape (pinned by the existing flow-stability deepEqual). PROOF: CrashBeforeReopenAuditStore injects a throw on exactly the reopen audit append inside the REAL runStoryTransition path (fault injection, not fixture state). RED in an isolated scratch copy: the pre-fix tree COMPILES CLEAN (build exit 0, so tsc cannot catch this class) while the smoke exits 1 at the assertion that a crash must leave a durable recovery record - reproducing the unrecoverable state; GREEN (exit 0) after restoring only the orchestrator. Verifier assertions proven to bite: 12 of 13 mutations flipped exit 0 to 1 with the expected message (record attached after the write, record given its own second write, call site drops reopenAuditId, guard not negated, guard removed, matching on reason text, clear before append, entry reconcile removed, record never attached, never cleared, drill defined-but-not-run, full registry-rationale revert); the single non-biting mutation removed only 1 of 3 occurrences of a token that a whole-rationale includes check correctly still matched. Verification: build 0, test:process-fact-contract 0, plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke 0, flow-stability-smoke 0, plus cli-e2e 0, review-convergence-smoke 0, review-loop-smoke 0. RESIDUALS STATED HONESTLY IN THE CODE DOCBLOCK, NOT GLOSSED: (1) the two-write window is made RECOVERABLE, not eliminated - after a crash the reason is durable immediately and only the event can be late; (2) recovery fires on the next TRANSITION, not on arbitrary read-only commands, because store.readStory sits in core/store.ts outside this story's permitted scope - until then the reason sits visibly on the index and no phase change can slip past it; (3) the already-audited check is read-then-append rather than an atomic CAS, serialized by the per-story transition lock, so it is exact under the same threat model as the persist claim and inherits its documented OS-freeze residual, whose failure mode is a DUPLICATE event sharing one auditId (dedupable) and never a lost one. Separately noted: transition-integrity-smoke fails identically on unmodified HEAD (pre-existing, not caused by this change, and not in the routine npm test chain).

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts:1428 (story_discard) breaks the invariant 'no phase change can follow an unaudited reopen' stated at packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:604. story_discard mutates story.phase directly (line 1428: story.phase = 'DISCARDED'; store.writeStory at ~1436) and never calls reconcilePendingReopenAudit and never routes through runStoryTransitionInner. Reproduced empirically: crash-inject the reopen audit append exactly like plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts does (phase=INIT + pendingReopenAudit committed on the worktree branch, zero audit events on disk), then instead of retrying story_advance, run story_discard --force from inside the worktree. Result: the worktree+branch (the ONLY place holding the pendingReopenAudit record) is force-deleted, the story silently reaches phase=DISCARDED (a terminal state with no outgoing machine edges), and NO audit event is EVER produced for a reopen that genuinely committed -- with zero warning to the operator. This also falsifies the documented residual at transition-orchestrator.ts ~975 ("Recovery fires on the next TRANSITION for the story (the only thing that can move a story out of INIT)... deferred, not lost"): story_discard is another thing that moves a story out of INIT without reconciling, and the loss here is PERMANENT, not deferred. A structurally identical blind spot exists at packages/main/src/handlers/story-query.ts:796 (the zombie-story DONE-reconcile path: story.phase = 'DONE' + store.writeStory with no reconciliation call), lower practical likelihood but same class of gap. Fix direction: call reconcilePendingReopenAudit at the top of every out-of-band phase-mutating handler (story_discard, the zombie DONE-reconcile path), and/or add a lattice doctor check that fails loudly when a story index still carries pendingReopenAudit with no matching process event, so the loss is surfaced rather than silent.

packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts reconcilePendingReopenAudit: the exact-auditId-vs-reason-text idempotency distinction (code comment states two reopens MAY legitimately share a reason) is enforced only by the AST contract check in verify-process-fact-contract.mjs, not by any executable test. Independently verified in an isolated scratch clone: mutating the already-audited match from event.reopenAuditId===pending.auditId to event.reason===pending.reason keeps build clean and both plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js and flow-stability-smoke.js fully GREEN (only test:process-fact-contract catches it). No drill exercises two reopens on the same story sharing an identical reason with different auditIds, so the documented same-reason edge case has zero executable regression coverage.
